title: Stylized Concept Art Meets 3D: How Marvelous Designer Enhances Illustration in Civilization 7
content:
## _Discover how artists like_[ _Ryan Andrade_](https://www.artstation.com/ryanandrade) _use Marvelous Designer to elevate concept art—combining 3D cloth simulation with traditional illustration techniques to create dramatic, painterly visuals for games like Civilization 7. From dynamic character poses to time-saving workflows, Marvelous Designer bridges the gap between realism and stylization in modern game development._

* * *

# **Interview with**[**Ryan Andrade**](https://www.artstation.com/ryanandrade)**| Civilization 7 | Lead Concept Artist at Firaxis**

# **Can you tell us a bit about yourself and your work on Civilization 7?**

![77b9152e98a4438cad07da520233a33a](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202506/0c35626a8bb045d9913382c279c8ce43/images/77b9152e98a4438cad07da520233a33aCopy%20of%20FranceLP_Thumbnail.jpg) My concept artwork has always had a heavy emphasis on 3D. I picked up Marvelous Designer back in 2014-ish when I was in college. I started using Marvelous Designer as a reference for painting more believable clothing folds for illustrations, and that’s essentially how I use it now on Civilization.

# **Civilization 7 features a stylized look. What led you to incorporate Marvelous Designer into your workflow, and how did it support the artistic direction?**

![bd2095716f384fda8836991994d459c6](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202506/0c35626a8bb045d9913382c279c8ce43/images/bd2095716f384fda8836991994d459c6Copy%20of%20XerxesLP_Thumb.jpg) Civ 7’s aesthetic is dark and moody, and our art director had tons of chiaroscuro paintings for us to reference early in production. Baroque and Renaissance era painters are masters of clothing folds (amongst many other things), and so I once again turned to Marvelous Designer to serve as my reference. Those old masters of course hired models to pose for days while they painted, later painters like Norman Rockwell would use photo reference of hired models for the same effect. For my purposes, I see Marvelous Designer as an evolution on that, allowing me to dress and pose characters which then inform my illustrations.

# **Workflow & Tools – Could you walk us through the key tools and software you used throughout the project?**

The first step often happens in Blender where I’m blocking out loose composition ideas with simple geometry. From there I’ll use Daz for more articulated and detailed characters, and put those characters in Marvelous Designer for cloth simulation. Then it’s back to Blender for lights & materials, and lastly is Photoshop for making brushy paint strokes.

# **Can you share some standout moments where Marvelous Designer played a crucial role in creating iconic scenes or characters?**

![c99c92dc2fe448bba83c11e3aaf6251a](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202506/0c35626a8bb045d9913382c279c8ce43/images/c99c92dc2fe448bba83c11e3aaf6251aCopy%20of%20FranceLP.jpg)_1) final painting_  


The French layer painting for Civ 7 was one of my favorite use cases for Marvelous. The focal point is a woman in a dress hoisting a flag in really dramatic lighting, which would have been hard to paint from scratch without 3D. The great thing about Marvelous is when you’re able to re-use and tweak older assets for new projects, in this case I already made 90% of the stuff I needed, which saved a lot of time.

![c98c161f97374a2083f7e7b5eee0bd87](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202506/0c35626a8bb045d9913382c279c8ce43/images/c98c161f97374a2083f7e7b5eee0bd87Copy%20of%20FranceLP_Process.jpg)_2) underpainting made using the 3D as a reference_

![2896955048b4439482a53ee5c208dd8e](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202506/0c35626a8bb045d9913382c279c8ce43/images/2896955048b4439482a53ee5c208dd8eCopy%20of%20FranceLP_Process2.jpg) _3) raw render from Blender using Marvelous Designer and Daz for the figures_  


The Xerxes illustration was a similar scenario, with tons of robed figures right up in front of the camera. Using Marvelous along with Blender gave me a solid foundation for my painting.

![30eeaee8c31546d7927a31174fba68fc](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202506/0c35626a8bb045d9913382c279c8ce43/images/30eeaee8c31546d7927a31174fba68fcCopy%20of%20XerxesLP.jpg)_1) Final painting_

![5e8b394b4175451ab9611e17aff0a32f](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202506/0c35626a8bb045d9913382c279c8ce43/images/5e8b394b4175451ab9611e17aff0a32fCopy%20of%20XerxesProcess.jpg) _2) raw render from Blender using Marvelous Designer & Daz for the figures_

# **What advice would you give to artists who want to use Marvelous Designer for concept art?**

Budget your time wisely, at least for professional work. Decide which characters in a scene will benefit most from detailed cloth sim, and which could make do without.

# **How would you describe your experience working with Marvelous Designer on this project?**

Marvelous is my go-to cloth simulation tool, I’ve used it for all sorts of personal and professional projects, and so far no other program comes close to matching its features.

#

title: Mariée de Kumya — Recreating Lolita Dress in Marvelous Designer 🎀
content:
## _Ever wondered how a highly detailed Lolita dress is made in 3D?_

## _From layered frills to hand-crafted bows, 3D Character Artist Honghui Qiu shares how he brought "Mariée de Kumya" Lolita dress to life with Marvelous Designer — and the challenges that came with it._

* * *

# **Interview with**[**Honghui Qiu**](https://www.artstation.com/qhhkkkk)[****](https://www.artstation.com/florencianespola1)**|**[**Mariée de Kumya Lolita Dress**](https://www.artstation.com/artwork/q)**| 3D Character Artist**

* * *

# **Please introduce yourself to the Marvelous Designer community.**

Hello everyone! My name is Qiu Honghui, a 3D character artist from China. I've been working in the game industry for two and a half years.

I was first introduced to 3D during a university course and found it incredibly fascinating. That initial spark led me to dive deeper into self-learning. However, I soon realized that 3D creation was far more complex than I had imagined. After graduating, I spent six months in a professional training program, which helped me gain the skills needed to enter the game industry.

# **What inspired you to create this piece? Could you share the story behind it?**

The inspiration came from a Lolita fashion show I stumbled upon on Bilibili. I was struck by how exquisitely detailed each outfit was, which sparked my interest in learning more about Lolita fashion.

This particular design is based on the 2023 “Mariée de Kumya” (Bear Bride) dress by Baby, The Stars Shine Bright. I was fascinated by its rich design elements — lace, embroidery, pearls, and satin, especially the intricate layering around the neckline, cuffs, and hem. I felt that recreating it in 3D could truly highlight its elegance and craftsmanship.

![c21e02d300f54369a28c86285d8a2696](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202506/fc8a1ec901504001bda74fd0f890409b/images/c21e02d300f54369a28c86285d8a2696%E7%86%8A%E7%86%8A%E8%8A%B1%E5%AB%81%E8%8D%89%E8%8E%93%E5%9B%AD%20%E5%AE%9E%E7%89%A9.jpg)![471ec7e5defd440fa8d7944aaa3f1c7f](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202506/fc8a1ec901504001bda74fd0f890409b/images/471ec7e5defd440fa8d7944aaa3f1c7f%E4%BD%9C%E5%93%81%E5%B1%95%E7%A4%BA12.jpg)

# **This Lolita design includes many intricate details such as layered patterns, bows, and lace trims. How did Marvelous Designer help improve your workflow or enable unique design effects?**

When working with multiple layers in Marvelous Designer, I use the **Layer** feature to define the hierarchy of each pattern. I also rely on **Deactivate** and **Freeze** functions to adjust layers individually.

![eaa475663865471daf92400dd1591168](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202506/fc8a1ec901504001bda74fd0f890409b/images/eaa475663865471daf92400dd1591168MD%E6%88%AA%E5%9B%BE02.png)

Creating lace trims is also very efficient in Marvelous Designer. I typically adjust the pattern length or modify the **weft/warp shrinkage ratio** to achieve lace-like effects, and sometimes use the **pleats and fold** tools to create textures similar to pleated skirts.

![3fec3db6c7054d3389cbc9bfe34e7e76](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202506/fc8a1ec901504001bda74fd0f890409b/images/3fec3db6c7054d3389cbc9bfe34e7e76MD%E6%88%AA%E5%9B%BE01.png)![e76341eebdbd4bad8c3dcaa39ce22032](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202506/fc8a1ec901504001bda74fd0f890409b/images/e76341eebdbd4bad8c3dcaa39ce22032%E4%BD%9C%E5%93%81%E5%B1%95%E7%A4%BA03.jpg)![b5f1aae341e34b93918128849a3db362](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202506/fc8a1ec901504001bda74fd0f890409b/images/b5f1aae341e34b93918128849a3db362%E4%BD%9C%E5%93%81%E5%B1%95%E7%A4%BA07.jpg)

The bows featured on the Lolita dress were all made using Marvelous Designer. One major advantage of using the software for bow creation is the flexibility to quickly model different styles based on your needs. I often use the **Fold Arrangement** tool and fine-tune details by adjusting the **fold angle** along internal lines.

![14f125bf835b490290623c56a906957e](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202506/fc8a1ec901504001bda74fd0f890409b/images/14f125bf835b490290623c56a906957e%E4%BD%9C%E5%93%81%E5%B1%95%E7%A4%BA09.jpg)![06538a62d14646b0b3221f9a87b649d8](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202506/fc8a1ec901504001bda74fd0f890409b/images/06538a62d14646b0b3221f9a87b649d8%E4%BD%9C%E5%93%81%E5%B1%95%E7%A4%BA11.jpg)![16e16f7698d648d19916443025e6c80c](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202506/fc8a1ec901504001bda74fd0f890409b/images/16e16f7698d648d19916443025e6c80c%E4%BD%9C%E5%93%81%E5%B1%95%E7%A4%BA10.jpg)

# **Did you encounter any challenges during the creation process? How did you overcome them?**

The main challenge I faced was with the **skirt**. Due to its large surface area and the layering of multiple pattern pieces, the CPU simulation became quite laggy. Additionally, it was difficult to achieve the exact volume and shape I had envisioned for the skirt.

To resolve this, I worked on the skirt separately in a dedicated project file, and went through **multiple iterations** adjusting the structure of the **petticoat**. I also fine-tuned the **fabric properties** for each layered piece individually. These steps eventually helped me reach a satisfying result.

![d0f30adc247d4eee8d4ca45c24d7848d](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202506/fc8a1ec901504001bda74fd0f890409b/images/d0f30adc247d4eee8d4ca45c24d7848d%E4%BD%9C%E5%93%81%E5%B1%95%E7%A4%BA01.jpg)

# **Could you briefly walk us through the tools and software you used during this project? Was Marvelous Designer well integrated into your workflow?**

I began with **Marvelous Designer** to create the garments during the modeling phase. The assets were then imported into **Blender** , where I performed **retopology** , added **edge bindings** , and created accessories.

For the texturing process, I used **Substance Designer** to craft the fabric patterns and materials. Final rendering was done in **Blender**.

Overall, the workflow between Marvelous Designer and Blender was very smooth and efficient.

![ef14418d53db452cac24563c97a54f23](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202506/fc8a1ec901504001bda74fd0f890409b/images/ef14418d53db452cac24563c97a54f23%E4%BD%9C%E5%93%81%E5%B1%95%E7%A4%BA13.jpg)![3c3f6403046e49508b51cab8dff65573](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202506/fc8a1ec901504001bda74fd0f890409b/images/3c3f6403046e49508b51cab8dff65573%E4%BD%9C%E5%93%81%E5%B1%95%E7%A4%BA17.jpg)![63f5e08df7a94c6192087e05d0fe6160](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202506/fc8a1ec901504001bda74fd0f890409b/images/63f5e08df7a94c6192087e05d0fe6160%E4%BD%9C%E5%93%81%E5%B1%95%E7%A4%BA14.jpg)![074d8dd9ebd8403697a84b59b61c0a9c](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202506/fc8a1ec901504001bda74fd0f890409b/images/074d8dd9ebd8403697a84b59b61c0a9c%E4%BD%9C%E5%93%81%E5%B1%95%E7%A4%BA15.jpg)![b05303d935dc4714b822857f9c9583f5](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202506/fc8a1ec901504001bda74fd0f890409b/images/b05303d935dc4714b822857f9c9583f5%E4%BD%9C%E5%93%81%E5%B1%95%E7%A4%BA16.jpg)

# **Do you have any advice for beginners who want to create a Lolita-style outfit using Marvelous Designer?**

My first piece of advice would be to **use a higher-spec computer** , as creating detailed Lolita garments can be quite demanding on system performance, especially when dealing with multiple layers and heavy simulations.

Also, it’s very helpful to collect **high-quality references** of Lolita designs. I’d like to recommend my mentor, **JueFei Kay20000** — you can check out his ArtStation portfolio here:[_https://kay20000.artstation.com_](https://kay20000.artstation.com)

# **How has your overall experience with Marvelous Designer been? Are there any improvements or new features you’d like to see in the future?**

This piece was created in 2023, when GPU simulation optimization hadn’t been introduced yet — so the process was relatively slow.

However, with continuous updates, Marvelous Designer has made **significant improvements** in performance. I recently saw the feature highlights for **Marvelous Designer 2025.0** , and I’m especially looking forward to the **redesigned UI** and the **quick-access asset store** , both of which I believe will greatly enhance workflow efficiency.

![8f6558a981fe405691b3dc24aa1f9122](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202506/fc8a1ec901504001bda74fd0f890409b/images/8f6558a981fe405691b3dc24aa1f9122%E4%BD%9C%E5%93%81%E5%B1%95%E7%A4%BA04.jpg)

title: Unlocking VMOD Magic Outside CLO: Fur Strand Breakthrough!
content:
* * *

Hi everyone!  
I’m **beyond excited** to share something I just discovered that completely **changed my workflow** – and I _had_ to post it here because I know I can’t be the only one who needed this!

🔍 I’ve always loved working with **VMODs** for fabrics in CLO, but as someone who renders mainly in external software (Unreal, Blender, etc.), I always felt limited – like I was missing the full power of those textures outside of CLO. Until now.

✨ I started experimenting with **Fur Strands inside VMODs** , and the results blew my mind. Turns out, you can totally **bake strand-based effects directly into the 3D model** , and then render them outside of CLO – without rebuilding the entire shader from scratch. No more starting from zero to simulate that delicate fiber look!

* * *

🔄 Before & After – Render Comparison

![1909bd239af846589b549ce418e393bd](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202505/2014fe3da04741ff949f9c1465d403b7/images/1909bd239af846589b549ce418e393bd1.png)**Left:** VMOD 3D with Fur Strand  
**Right:** Original VMOD 3D  
What’s crazy is this used to be **just a render-time effect**. But now… it’s **actual geometry inside the 3D view**! No tricks, no illusions – those fibers are **real mesh strands** you can see and work with before even hitting render.

* * *

### 🧵 True 3D Vision – No More “Render-Only” Magic

![41a5e9f5e5e7453185cdf320e069adf4](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202505/2014fe3da04741ff949f9c1465d403b7/images/41a5e9f5e5e7453185cdf320e069adf42.png)

On the left: **VMOD with Fur Strand** – you can clearly see the strand geometry right inside the 3D viewport.  
On the right: Original VMOD – the texture is there, but it’s just a visual placeholder until render.  
  
And here’s the amazing part:

🔁 **Once you copy over the fur settings** (shape, density, roughness map, etc.),  
🎯 The **final render looks almost identical** to the original!  
But now you’re working with actual geometry — not a preset shader effect that only comes alive at render time.

This opens up a whole new world of flexibility:  
✅ You can preview and tweak fur in real time.  
✅ Export it to external engines like Unreal or Blender.  
✅ And finally bridge the gap between **hyperrealism and workflow control**.  


* * *

### 💡 Why This Matters (at least to me!)

This discovery means:

  * I can **re-use** my entire library of custom VMODs outside CLO.

  * No need to rebuild complex shaders in other tools.

  * Textures look **richer, fuzzier, and closer to real fabric** , especially for knits, fleece, and delicate materials.




Honestly, it felt like unlocking a **secret power-up**. If you’ve ever wanted to push the realism of your renders while keeping a smooth pipeline, **this is for you**.

* * *

### 🔧 Super Tip!

When transitioning from _Fur Render_ (render-only) to _Fur Strand_ (real-time), some settings reset or behave differently — but with a few adjustments, you can recreate the original look or even enhance it.

Here’s my personal checklist and advanced tips after testing:

✅ **Base, Normal, Metallic, Displacement texture**  
→ This is preserved. No changes needed.

⚠️ **Fur parameters**  
→ These reset, so you’ll need to reapply:

  * Hair shape

  * Shine

  * Gravity

  * Curl

  * Variation

  * **Roughness** → Switch from value to **map** input for more accurate surface behavior.

  * **Density & Seed** → Play with different seed settings to discover subtle or dramatic variations. A single seed change can alter the entire flow without touching the base design.




🌓 **Opacity Map**  
→ I recommend **increasing contrast** , especially in darker areas, to restore the sense of translucency and depth seen in the original render. Without this, the material can look flat or less realistic.

🧩 **Custom Density Mapping (Advanced)**  
→ If your fabric has different fur behavior in specific areas (e.g. front vs. sides), unlink them:

  * Separate the textile into **front and side sections** using the properties editor

  * This lets you control **density, length, and hair direction** by faces.




* * *

### 🗣️ I’d love to hear from others:

Have you tried integrating strand-based textures into your external workflow?  
Any tips, feedback, or renders you want to share?

  
👀 Can you tell which one this is?  
  
![fbd6d41e40ae4f5c973bdb717e841ef8](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202505/2014fe3da04741ff949f9c1465d403b7/images/fbd6d41e40ae4f5c973bdb717e841ef8VMOD%203D%20ORIGINAL.png)

Thanks for reading!  
— Seer  
![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202505/2014fe3da04741ff949f9c1465d403b7/images/a356275c837f4137ac1e77ca099f22c63.png)

title: IconX Shortfilm
content:
## _Get an inside look at how Them Studio brought a fresh metaverse vision to life—merging cutting-edge visuals with heartfelt storytelling and a stylized aesthetic that pushes the boundaries of commercial CG work using Marvelous Designer for stylized animation._

* * *

# **Interview with**[**THEM Studio**](https://www.behance.net/gallery/212722569/IconX-Shortfilm)

# **To start off, could you introduce yourself and your team at IconX Studio?**

Hey everyone! I’m [Dima Havryliv](https://www.instagram.com/dima_gavriliv/), and I was the art director on this project as part of the team at Them Studio. We’re a group of bold, forward-thinking artists based in Kyiv. Each of us has strong experience as a solo CG artist, but when we join forces, we’re able to create truly exciting work — and this project is a great example of that. We’re really excited to share it with you.  


At Them Studio, we create a wide range of 3D visuals — from large-screen video content to product-focused animations. But recently, we’ve become especially interested in short films. Inspired by Spider Verse, we decided to explore a new style for ourselves, combining 2D and 3D elements. That inspiration turned into a creative journey that led to this project.

![c1a2240c9475463e89c98378ae58795d](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202505/9c36cccf061448ae9b8a9cc721380b11/images/c1a2240c9475463e89c98378ae58795dBehancePage.png)

# **What inspired the concept behind this short film? Can you tell us how the idea first came about and developed?**

This was a commercial project — the client wanted to present a metaverse concept, but in a fresh and emotionally engaging way. The goal was to evoke a feeling before revealing the product itself. We were given a general direction, but had a lot of creative freedom in how to bring it to life.

We started with a storyboard, where we defined the narrative and visual tone of the film. As I mentioned earlier, our team was deeply inspired by Spider-Verse, and we were excited to experiment with integrating a similar aesthetic — blending 2D and 3D elements in a stylized way.

There were definitely challenges, especially during the R&D stage, where we tested our ideas to see if they could actually work in motion. Once we locked in the visual style and got approval on the storyline with our main character, we jumped into production.

![a5ea7c42466c4ad2ae75e64697603443](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202505/9c36cccf061448ae9b8a9cc721380b11/images/a5ea7c42466c4ad2ae75e64697603443ClothConcept.png)

# **What led you to choose Marvelous Designer for this project? In what ways did it support your artistic vision?**

Even though most of us come from a Cinema 4D background — and Maxon has introduced some strong cloth simulation updates — we still prefer using Marvelous Designer. It’s much more intuitive and consistently delivers better results when it comes to clothing.

It played a key role in this project, especially since our character’s outfit was a crucial part of their identity and visual presence. From the beginning, we knew that if we were going to include a character, the clothing couldn’t be an afterthought — it had to be designed with care and purpose. Marvelous Designer helped us achieve exactly that.

![918644c3fe704fd3ad705117be6169b6](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202505/9c36cccf061448ae9b8a9cc721380b11/images/918644c3fe704fd3ad705117be6169b6outfit04.png)![be714a244a5d42baa3209cd363d1ad1b](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202505/9c36cccf061448ae9b8a9cc721380b11/images/be714a244a5d42baa3209cd363d1ad1bpattern01.png)

![edf613fd2bf84303838bca541bb6c59b](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202505/9c36cccf061448ae9b8a9cc721380b11/images/edf613fd2bf84303838bca541bb6c59boutfit03.png)

![26b18493574d429fb6b2c2486c219779](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202505/9c36cccf061448ae9b8a9cc721380b11/images/26b18493574d429fb6b2c2486c219779pattern04.png)![115d1fb4f8514e67938352955eeba667](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202505/9c36cccf061448ae9b8a9cc721380b11/images/115d1fb4f8514e67938352955eeba667Stillshots02.png)![934eded4323747e5b7c9ac5a73dda57f](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202505/9c36cccf061448ae9b8a9cc721380b11/images/934eded4323747e5b7c9ac5a73dda57fpattern02.png)

# **We’re particularly curious about the scene where Robert jumps out the window in slow motion, yet his clothes flow naturally. How did you simulate that moment using Marvelous Designer? Any tips you'd like to share?**

![3da0a19fec3749e49243af5028c54ae7](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202505/9c36cccf061448ae9b8a9cc721380b11/images/3da0a19fec3749e49243af5028c54ae7Stillshots03.png)

Let me pass this one over to [_Egor Haiev_](https://connect.clo-set.com/community/post/403e71fa0f57448a998c342871f5221d), a member of our team who was directly responsible for that simulation:

**_"This simulation was arguably one of the most challenging. I’d say it took me around 40 attempts to figure out exactly which settings needed to be adjusted to achieve a realistic result._**

**_The key parameter, in my opinion, was Scene Time Warp. What I discovered is that the higher the value, the more the sequence gets stretched out, which allows Marvelous Designer to calculate additional in-between frames. For example, in the scene where the character jumps out of the window, I set this value to around 50 to help compensate for the high speed of the jump._**

**_A small tip for users: if you notice that part of the fabric clips through the character or behaves oddly, you can pause the simulation at that moment, freeze the clothing elements that are working correctly, and leave only the problematic part active. Then, re-run the simulation in the viewport to fix just that area. Once it’s resolved, unfreeze the rest and continue the sim._**

**_This approach lets you preserve the overall animation—including inertia—while focusing on smaller problem areas. And if glitches continue, the same process can be repeated."_**

![63a704ac44f74885a9d37e6d2580d221](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202505/9c36cccf061448ae9b8a9cc721380b11/images/63a704ac44f74885a9d37e6d2580d2211.gif)

# **Could you walk us through the main tools you used in your pipeline for this animation project?**

For this animation project, our main tool was Cinema 4D with the Redshift engine. All of the scenes were built in C4D, including texturing, lighting, and materials. Most of the work was done within this software.

For certain scenes, such as the window jump scene, where we used a 2D background, we found that Blender handled 2D perspectives better, so we used it specifically for those parts.

Marvelous Designer was essential for creating the character’s clothing, allowing us to achieve realistic and dynamic fabric simulation.

For character design, we used Character Creator to build the main character.

The character animation was done in Maya, where we specifically worked at 12 fps to give the project a more cartoonish, stylized feel.

Photoshop was used for the additional stylization of textures and to add 2D motion blur effects and inserts during post-production.

Finally, all of the visual effects, color grading, and anything that enhanced our 3D visuals were brought together in After Effects for post-production.

# **What were some of the key challenges you faced while working with Marvelous Designer?**

Since this wasn’t our first time working with Marvelous Designer, creating the clothing itself wasn’t a major challenge. However, given that our video uses 12 fps for the character animation — a stylistic choice — we were a bit concerned about potential issues with the simulation.

Surprisingly, everything went smoothly. We increased the time calculation, which helped, and the results looked great. After that, we brought the Alembic file into Cinema 4D, removed every second frame, and the animation held up perfectly.

# **Do you have any advice for artists looking to use Marvelous Designer for stylized animation projects?**

_Egor Haiev_

"I believe that the quality of the character animation plays a significant role. Fortunately, we had a very talented animator on our team, which contributed to the overall dynamic and lifelike feel of the project. However, the clothing itself should not be overlooked. While the overall style is certainly important, it's often the small details that add an extra layer of interest.

In Robert’s case, I would highlight his concert outfit—particularly the jacket with the strap that sways nicely with the character’s movements. A similar feature appears in his main outfit, the one he wears during the window jump scene. There, it's the layered nature of the clothing that stands out. We found the overlapping of several garments in that context to be quite visually compelling"

# **Finally, how would you sum up your overall experience using Marvelous Designer throughout this project?**

It was an exciting adventure, but without the clothes, it would’ve been pretty cold and tough! We’ve used Marvelous Designer before, and in this project, it truly became a key part of the process. Big thanks to the team for making sure our character stayed stylish while we animated them!
